text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: `redis-maxclients` -> https://pagerduty.com/alerts/P12345
PagerDuty: Incident #INC-98765 triggered by redis cluster 'cache-prod-1' - paging primary oncall.

sam: ack'd the page :white_check_mark: (sam reclaimed)
sam: seeing a spike in redis CLIENT LIST and 'maxclients reached' errors in logs. App errors ~ 5% 503s, mostly writes.
lee: digging in metrics now — Netstat shows many CLOSE_WAIT from app host pool. Redis used_clients ~ 10234, maxclients=10000 (from config).
lee: paste of recent redis warnings from logs:
```
[2026-05-03T04:12:11Z] WARNING: Accepted client connection but could not allocate client struct - maxclients reached
[2026-05-03T04:12:12Z] ERR: Client attempted command but server denied - maxclients
```

maria: ok, initial mitigation options: 1) throttle non-critical background jobs, 2) enable read-only failover to replica for reads, 3) temporarily release app-side connection pool backpressure (reduce pool size to force queueing), 4) increase redis maxclients and restart or scale redis.
sam: quick check — how many connections per app dyno? dave: roughly 25 per worker, 300 workers across fleet -> ~7500 connections, plus other services ~2k. That aligns.
dave: running `redis-cli INFO clients` now:
```
# Clients
connected_clients:10234
client_longest_output_list:0
client_biggest_input_buf:0
blocked_clients:12
```

lee: replica lag 0.3s, so safe to divert reads for now. I'll flip read traffic on a small % canary to replicas.
maria: do that for 10% first, watch 5xx rate and latency. Also create a temporary key TTL cache for high-frequency write paths.
sam: initiating throttle for background jobs via k8s scale to 0 for noncritical-jobs namespace.
dave: scaled job controller to 0, pushed a runtime feature flag to reduce polling. Jobs should stop generating redis load.
sam: doing a rolling restart of a subset of app pods to reclaim leaked connections (graceful drain). Command:
```bash
kubectl rollout restart deployment/frontend -n prod --timeout=5m
```

incident-bot: automation note: escalated to db-sre if no ack from DB team in 5m.
lee: increasing read traffic to replicas to 12% now (canary). Monitoring.
maria: while that stabilizes, we should raise maxclients on cache-prod-1 to 15000 and plan a refresh window — need kernel ulimit changes; can't hotpatch safely without restart on current infra. Suggest scale out redis nodes instead to add capacity without restart.
dave: starting scale plan: create one additional redis shard node and rebalance a few high-card keys. Running terraform apply for new replica pool now.
sam: customer impact assessment: ~5% of requests returned 503s over last 10m, mostly write-heavy customers (billing and real-time notifications). No full outages reported. Notifying support with temp mitigation and ETA for capacity increase.
PagerDuty: Reminder - if acknowledgement window > 20m escalate to senior oncall.
lee: can we also reduce app-side idle timeouts? Some clients hang open and inflate client count. I'll push a config change to drop idle after 30s.
dave: applied idle timeout change to connection pool (frontend config) and restarted a small subset, observing connection drop-offs.
maria: metrics: 503 rate down to 1.2% after throttles and canary, p95 latency up slightly but within SLOs. Good sign.
sam: handing over to lee for DB/redis follow-up — I'll be offline for next 40m (meeting) but reachable by DM for critical.
lee: taking over incident lead. I'll coordinate with infra to finalize scale out and schedule a maintenance window for a controlled restart if needed.
lee: next steps logged in incident tracker: https://internal.incidents/redwood/INC-98765 — will attach timeline and mitigations.
incident-bot: Incident acknowledged by lee, pager duty notes updated.
PagerDuty: Incident acknowledged, no further automatic escalations planned.
lee: final note for now — we will finish scaling redis nodes and plan a low-traffic restart in 45m if numbers don't drop further. If anything spikes, ping me @sam and @maria. :lock:

(End of thread)
